claims.text: Adding approximately 1–4 at.% Cu to a high-entropy alloy will enhance its heat-transfer capability.
Adding approximately 1–4 at.% Cu will preserve the alloy's structural integrity under reactor intermediate-layer conditions.
Low-level Cu addition will produce fine Cu-rich precipitates or localized Cu segregation at grain boundaries.
Cu-rich grain-boundary features will act as conductive bridges along grain boundaries.
The proposed conductive bridges will improve phonon transport pathways.
The proposed conductive bridges will improve electron transport pathways.
Improved phonon and electron transport pathways will increase effective thermal conductivity without significantly degrading microstructural integrity.
The Cu-doped alloy will have approximately 10–20% higher effective thermal conductivity than the undoped alloy.
The Cu-doped alloy will experience only a minimal reduction in mechanical strength relative to the undoped alloy.
The predicted benefit will hold during thermal cycling at approximately 500–600°C under moderate mechanical loading.
The specified thermal and mechanical loading conditions are representative of plasma-facing reactor environments.
The beneficial effects are limited to Cu concentrations of approximately 1–4 at.%.
Higher Cu concentrations or more extreme operating conditions may cause adverse phase changes.
The magnitude of conductivity enhancement and the mechanical response depend on the alloy composition and processing parameters.
